stories.headline: SK hynix's Solidigm weighs first US NAND fab, with upstate New York the leading site

key_facts.fact: SK hynix's US subsidiary Solidigm is considering building a NAND flash memory factory in the United States, with upstate New York a leading candidate, three people familiar with the matter said on September 18.
key_facts.excerpt: Chipmaker SK Hynix's US subsidiary Solidigm is considering building a factory to manufacture NAND flash memory chips in the United States, with upstate New York a leading candidate for the site, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: The project is separate from SK hynix's parallel talks with Intel about making memory chips at Intel's Ohio facility.
key_facts.excerpt: The project would be separate from SK Hynix's discussions with Intel (INTC.O), opens new tab over manufacturing memory chips at Intel's Ohio facility, the sources said.

key_facts.fact: A US plant would cut Solidigm's dependence on its sole NAND production site in Dalian, China, and shield it from US tariffs and export curbs on chipmaking gear to China.
key_facts.excerpt: A U.S. plant would reduce Solidigm's reliance on its sole NAND production facility in the Chinese city of Dalian, while helping to shield it from potential U.S. tariffs and curbs on exports of chipmaking equipment to China.

key_facts.fact: Solidigm was created when SK hynix bought Intel's NAND business for $9 billion in late 2021; it currently runs only a headquarters and an R&D center in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Solidigm was launched as a separate entity when SK hynix acquired Intel's NAND business for $9 billion, or about 12 trillion won, in late 2021. Solidigm currently operates production facilities in Dalian, China, while running only its headquarters and a research and development center in the United States.

key_facts.fact: SK hynix is already spending more than $4 billion on an advanced HBM packaging plant in West Lafayette, Indiana; a front-end NAND line would be its first US wafer fab.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is investing more than $4 billion, or about 5.5293 trillion won, to build an advanced packaging plant in West Lafayette, Indiana.

key_facts.fact: SK hynix said Solidigm is 'reviewing various options to strengthen its business competitiveness, but no specific plans have been confirmed at this time.'
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix said its "subsidiary Solidigm is reviewing various options to strengthen its business competitiveness, but no specific plans have been confirmed at this time."

stories.headline: China's CXMT prepares a NAND flash push, taking on Samsung, SK hynix and YMTC

key_facts.fact: CXMT, China's leading DRAM maker, is preparing to enter the NAND flash memory market, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on September 18.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese chipmaker CXMT (688825.SS) is preparing to enter the booming flash memory chip market dominated by Samsung Electronics and other foreign rivals, three people with knowledge of the matter said, a move that would broaden its customer base amid a global memory shortage.

key_facts.fact: CXMT plans a NAND research-and-development production line at a new plant in Beijing and has set up a research institute in the capital where NAND development is among the projects.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT, also known as ChangXin Memory Technologies, plans to establish a research-and-development production line for NAND flash memory at its new plant in Beijing, according to two of the sources. The company has also set up a research institute in the Chinese capital and projects there include NAND development, one source said.

key_facts.fact: CXMT has already discussed its NAND plans with customers, including a newly established startup that wants to buy its NAND for storage products used in AI systems and supercomputers.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT has discussed its NAND plans with customers, including a newly established startup that intends to buy its NAND chips for storage products used in AI systems and supercomputers, a third person said, though they declined to identify the company.

key_facts.fact: SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung said in July that 2027 could be the memory industry's worst year from a supply perspective; TrendForce expects NAND tightness to ease only in the second half of next year.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung said in July that 2027 could be the industry's worst year from a supply perspective, while TrendForce expects NAND supply tightness to ease only in the second half of next year.

key_facts.fact: CXMT raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) in July in Asia's biggest IPO of the year and plans a second memory plant in Beijing.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT, which raised 57.92 billion yuan (US$8.6 billion) in July in Asia's biggest initial public offering this year, plans a second memory-chip plant in Beijing and was in funding talks with a tech manufacturing hub backed by the local government, Reuters reported last month.

key_facts.fact: CXMT shares rose 3.4% to 55.29 yuan on Friday after the report.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT shares rose 3.4% to CNY 55.29 on Friday after a Reuters report.

stories.headline: SK hynix launches a Silicon Valley venture arm targeting AI compute, data centers and optics

key_facts.fact: SK hynix announced on September 18 the launch of a corporate venture capital brand, 'SK hynix Ventures', to expand strategic partnerships across the global AI ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix Inc. (or "the company", www.skhynix.com) announced today the launch of its corporate venture capital (CVC) brand, "SK hynix Ventures," aimed at expanding strategic partnerships within the global AI ecosystem and securing future innovative technologies.

key_facts.fact: The brand was unveiled at the inaugural 'SK hynix Ventures Day' held in Silicon Valley on September 17 local time, attended by CEO Kwak Noh-jung, global VC firms and US AI-computing and data-center startups.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix announced on the 18th that it held its first "SK hynix Ventures Day" in Silicon Valley, U.S., on the 17th (local time), where it discussed future investment strategies and technical collaboration plans with global venture capital (VC) firms and startup representatives.

key_facts.fact: Investment scope widens from semiconductors and emerging tech to AI computing, data centers, system software and optical interconnect.
key_facts.excerpt: The new investment focus will cover areas including AI computing, data center infrastructure, system software and optical interconnect technologies, as SK hynix seeks opportunities in sectors expected to support AI applications.

key_facts.fact: SK hynix has run a CVC organization through its Americas unit SKHYA since 2015, investing in the US, China, Israel and Japan, with returns exceeding twice the cumulative amount invested.
key_facts.excerpt: Since 2015, SK hynix has operated a CVC organization through its Americas unit, SKHYA, investing directly in semiconductor and emerging-technology startups in the U.S., China, Israel and Japan and committing capital to venture funds. Returns so far have exceeded twice the cumulative amount invested.

key_facts.fact: CEO Kwak Noh-jung said competitiveness in the AI era 'stems not just from rapidly securing innovative technologies, but from ecosystem capabilities where customers, partners, and startups create new value together.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Competitiveness in the AI era stems not just from rapidly securing innovative technologies, but from ecosystem capabilities where customers, partners, and startups create new value together," said Kwak Noh-Jung, CEO of SK hynix.

stories.headline: Figure's Helix 2.5 does chores in 30 homes it never trained in, hitting 56% success

key_facts.fact: Figure announced Helix 2.5 on September 17, a neural network that let its humanoid perform whole-body household tasks across 30 unseen Bay Area homes with no data collection or model adaptation in those homes.
key_facts.excerpt: Figure introduced Helix 2.5, a neural network that enabled its humanoid robot to perform three whole-body household tasks across 30 unseen homes without collecting data or adapting the model in those environments.

key_facts.fact: The robots completed 237 of 420 trials, about 56%, across bed making, towel folding and tidying toys.
key_facts.excerpt: completed 237 of 420 trials, about 56%, across bed making, towel folding and tidying toys.

key_facts.fact: In a controlled comparison with identical task data and architecture, the Index-pretrained policy succeeded on 56% of trials versus 9% for a model trained from scratch.
key_facts.excerpt: In a controlled comparison using identical task data and model architecture, the Index-pretrained policy succeeded on 56% of trials, compared with 9% for the model trained from scratch.

key_facts.fact: Helix 2.5 halved the task-specific data needed to specify a behavior while expanding scope from one environment to 30 — 2x cheaper behavior specification, 30x deployment scope, per Figure.
key_facts.excerpt: Figure said Helix 2.5 cut the amount of task-specific data needed to specify a behavior in half while expanding its scope from a single environment to 30 unseen homes. The company described that as making behavior specification 2x cheaper while increasing its deployment scope 30x.

key_facts.fact: Figure says its Index data engine now generates about 35 minutes of human-experience data per second, and the company has committed $3.5 billion in compute to training Helix.
key_facts.excerpt: Figure pointed out that Index is generating about 35 minutes of new human-experience data every second. The company has also committed $3.5 billion in computing resources to training Helix.

key_facts.fact: CEO Brett Adcock called Helix 2.5 'the most important project we've ever taken on at Figure' and said the robot recorded successes in every one of the 30 homes.
key_facts.excerpt: In the accompanying video, Adcock calls Helix 2.5 "the most important project we've ever taken on at Figure." He and Director of AI Corey Lynch say the robot recorded successes in every one of the 30 homes.

stories.headline: D-Robotics raises $400M Series C for robot chips, China's biggest robotics round in four years

key_facts.fact: D-Robotics announced on September 17 the closing of a US$400 million Series C round, with a leading global internet company as a strategic investor alongside top-tier institutions and existing shareholders.
key_facts.excerpt: HONG KONG, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- D-Robotics, a leading provider of robotics development infrastructure, today announced the closing of a US$400 million Series C funding round. The round attracted strategic investment from a leading global internet company, alongside with top-tier investment institutions, and continued follow-on investments from existing shareholders.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Mirae Asset.
key_facts.excerpt: D-Robotics announced that it has secured $400 million in funding, led by Mirae Asset.

key_facts.fact: Proceeds go to expanding the Sunrise chip portfolio across all compute tiers and to a software platform spanning the full robot development chain.
key_facts.excerpt: The funding aims to enhance Sunrise™ Chip product portfolio across all computing levels, and to develop a software platform spanning the entire robot development chain.

key_facts.fact: D-Robotics has shipped over 8 million Sunrise chips, and its new S600 chip for embodied AI is used by more than 20 leading humanoid makers including UBTECH and Fourier.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has shipped over 8 million Sunrise chips and revenue grew several times year over year in the first half of 2026. Its new S600 chip for embodied AI is already used by more than 20 leading humanoid makers including UBTECH and Fourier.

key_facts.fact: The deal is described as the largest robotics funding round in China in the past four years.
key_facts.excerpt: D-Robotics, which is a leading provider of robotics development infrastructure in China, announced it has closed a $400 million Series C funding round. This is the largest robotics funding round in China in the past four years.

key_facts.fact: Its Gravity Program has backed more than 500 robotics innovators across 10 categories; over 100,000 developers in 20+ countries build on its platform.
key_facts.excerpt: To date, the program has backed more than 500 robotics innovators across 10 frontier categories... more than 500 universities and over 100,000 developers across 20+ countries have created hundreds of AI robot on the D-Robotics' platform.

stories.headline: Tesla places a 5,000-unit Optimus order and audits Chinese suppliers as mass production nears

key_facts.fact: News dated September 17 says Tesla recently issued a new order of about 5,000 Optimus units to suppliers — its first thousand-unit-scale mass production order after earlier trial orders of a few hundred.
key_facts.excerpt: News on September 17 shows that Tesla has recently issued a new order of about 5,000 units to its suppliers, which is the first mass production order at the thousand-unit level following the previous trial production orders of several hundred units.

key_facts.fact: Tesla is accelerating factory audits of its Optimus supply chain in China, visiting suppliers in Shanghai, Hangzhou, Ningbo and Xiamen.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla is accelerating the factory audit of the Optimus humanoid robot supply chain in China, visiting suppliers in Shanghai, Hangzhou, Ningbo and Xiamen and other regions. The dual signals of factory audit and order mark that Optimus has officially moved from the engineering prototype stage to the replicable manufacturing stage.

key_facts.fact: Tesla launched a production inspection for its humanoid robot business in Ningbo on September 16; Tuopu said it received no inspection notice while Sanhua Intelligent Controls said it is developing robotic joint actuators.
key_facts.excerpt: According to ChainCatcher, Tesla launched a production inspection for its humanoid robot business in Ningbo on September 16, issuing orders to supply chain partners. Topp Group stated it did not receive inspection notifications but confirmed ongoing collaboration in robot components, while Sanhua Intelligence Controls indicated it is developing robotic joint actuators.

key_facts.fact: Drone footage posted Thursday afternoon shows the steel frame of Tesla's dedicated Optimus factory at Giga Texas nearing completion, about six months after groundbreaking, with high-volume production targeted for summer 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla's dedicated Optimus factory at Gigafactory Texas is closing in on a finished steel frame, according to drone footage posted Thursday afternoon by longtime site observer Joe Tegtmeyer... Tesla has not given an updated timeline beyond its previously stated goal of bringing high volume Optimus production online at the site in the summer of 2027.

key_facts.fact: Musk has pegged long-term output at 10 million Optimus units a year at Giga Texas, versus a one-million-unit pilot line at Fremont that began mass producing the Gen 3 robot in January.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk has pegged the long term output target at 10 million Optimus units a year once the line is running at full capacity, a volume that would dwarf the one million unit pilot line Tesla is standing up separately at its Fremont, California factory.

stories.headline: AMD tells partners to expect ~10% price hikes in Q4 as TSMC raises wafer prices

key_facts.fact: AMD told partners on September 17 to expect a roughly 10% price increase on AI accelerators, Radeon GPUs and motherboard chipsets starting in Q4 2026, citing rising TSMC wafer costs, with Ryzen CPUs left off the list.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD told partners on September 17 to expect a roughly 10% price increase on AI accelerators, Radeon GPUs, and motherboard chipsets starting Q4 2026, citing rising TSMC wafer costs, but left Ryzen CPUs off the list.

key_facts.fact: TSMC has notified customers of an approximate 10% increase in wafer foundry quotes, citing persistently rising manufacturing costs.
key_facts.excerpt: According to supply chain information obtained by ChannelGate, TSMC—citing persistently rising manufacturing costs—has notified its customers of an approximate 10% increase in chip foundry quotes.

key_facts.fact: Intel has separately raised prices on select client and server chips — the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus up $50 to about $349 and the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus up $30 to about $229, with some Xeons up by hundreds or over $1,000.
key_facts.excerpt: For desktop, the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus and Core Ultra 5 250K Plus have recommended customer price increases of $50 and $30 respectively, bringing them to approximately $349 and $229. On the server side, Xeon processor increases are larger, with some models costing hundreds or even over $1,000 more than before.

key_facts.fact: On the same day, cloud provider Nebius raised AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rental rates by 25%.
key_facts.excerpt: The same day, cloud provider Nebius announced its own hikes, raising AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rental rates 25%, a sign AI compute demand still outstrips supply.

key_facts.fact: DRAM contract prices are already up 13%-18% quarter-on-quarter in Q3 2026, compounding cost pressure on PCs and servers.
key_facts.excerpt: | Memory | DRAM contract prices | +13%–18% QoQ | Q3 2026 |

key_facts.fact: AMD had not issued an official response to the price hike reports as of publication.
key_facts.excerpt: As of press time, AMD has not issued an official response to the price hike reports.
